entities.summary:
Palladas was a Greek poet, who lived in Alexandria, Egypt. He was born in the 5th century CE and died on May 17, 500 CE. Palladas' poetry is known for its lyricism and focus on themes of love, beauty, and nature. His works had a significant impact on the development of Byzantine literature.

Palladas' life was marked by his association with the Byzantine court, where he served as a poet laureate. He was also known for his translations of Greek myths into Latin.

Despite his influence on Byzantine literature, Palladas' work fell out of favor during the Middle Ages, only to be rediscovered in the Renaissance. Today, he is recognized as one of the greatest poets of the Byzantine Empire.

Palladas' legacy extends beyond his poetry, for it reflects the cultural and intellectual currents of the ancient world. His works continue to inspire scholars and writers to this day.
